title: world_scaffold/1
description: A NAMING call's output. The world's namespace: what exists, what it is called, what kind of thing it is, where it sits, and HOW MUCH OF IT SHOULD EXIST (relevance). Deliberately unable to express depth — no standing, no inner life, no description, no canon — because a schema that offers a field is an invitation to fill it, and prose in a naming call is the single largest cost in the fill (measured 2026-08-31: 62.8% of all output tokens, writing relevance-3 interiors on relevance-1 people). Depth is authored later, per entity, at the level this call assigns.

within.description: canonical_name of the place that contains this one. A world is nested: the largest thing the brief describes contains the next, down to the smallest place a body can stand in. Omit only for the outermost place.

relevance.description: How much of this thing exists (ADR-P027). 1 exists: a name, a descriptor and one tag. 2 referenced: enough to hold a scene. 3 interacted: the full interior, and an image. 4 bound to the player: as 3, with an asset nobody else may share. Author to the level you are given and no further — a relevance-1 entity is complete at 1, not a draft of a 3.

tag.description: The single characteristic thing about this entity that a narrator can play with in one line: a person's temperament, a faction's mantra or oath, a business's slogan, a concept's claim. This is what a relevance-1 entity answers from, so it carries the whole personality.
